source.title: Mitigating Early Training Collapse in CTR Models

page_placements.theme: One-epoch overfitting with sparse categorical embeddings

record.tranche_reason: It reports validation behavior across training epochs in industrial CTR settings, conceptually bearing on epoch-wise double descent, but does not reproduce the original experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an epoch-wise validation-performance pattern and training-duration outcomes for sparsity interventions. Figure 1 is described as an illustration, not a measured result. The paper does not sweep model size or sample size.
record.test_reason: The study is about one-epoch overfitting in CTR models: validation AUC peaks after epoch 1 and then degrades. It reports no per-epoch error curve and no training past the overfitting point. Nothing locates an interpolation threshold or looks for a second descent. It cites Belkin et al. only to frame Figure 1, which is illustrative, as a 'U-shaped training regime'. Its results are mitigation outcomes (AUC, log-loss, PRAUC, epoch counts) for sparsity interventions. None of these bears on whether any double-descent version holds. The early peak and decline is ordinary overfitting, a related but different construct. It is not evidence against V2, because the study never trains or reports far enough to show whether a second descent occurs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that early training collapse is primarily driven by feature sparsity rather than optimization dynamics alone. They find that removing sparse features and aggregating rare values improves stability, enables multi-epoch training, and lifts offline and online metrics, while lowering the learning rate gives limited benefit.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines early validation degradation in industrial CTR models and feature-sparsity interventions; it does not reproduce the original model-size or interpolation-threshold experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported mitigation outcomes differ by intervention: reducing the learning rate gives only incremental gains, while sparse-feature removal extends stable training to multiple epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep CTR models are described as peaking in validation performance after one epoch and degrading thereafter. Removing sparse features or filtering rare values reportedly extends useful training (Epochs 2 to 3–4 and 2–3) and improves AUC and log-loss more than lowering the learning rate does.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: One-epoch overfitting in CTR models is driven by categorical-feature sparsity, and reducing sparsity extends useful multi-epoch training.

record.problems: The measured datasets and model identities are not specified. The reported epoch-wise validation pattern has no numerical per-epoch results, and Figure 1 is illustrative. The table does not define its Epochs column or report uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: Offline AUC, log-loss and PRAUC summary values and online performance improvements were not included: they do not report the epoch-wise error shape tested by V2.

untested.parts: The whole version: no measured epoch-wise test-error curve, no long training, no interpolation threshold, no second descent examined.
No capacity sweep across model classes.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V2 'challenges' label is removed. The absence of a reported second descent reflects that the study never looked for one, not a measured absence. Datasets and models are unnamed, there is no uncertainty, and Table 1's Epochs column is undefined.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error measurement by model size.
No reported second descent in validation performance after the early decline; no detailed per-epoch numerical curve.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is evaluated as a predictor of peak location.
The study does not test label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison against an effective parameter count.

statements.correction: Validation performance reportedly peaks after epoch 1. Table 1 Epochs: baseline 2; Lower LR 2; Feature Removal 3–4; Value Filtering 2–3. Column meaning unspecified. Section 3.1 reports stable multi-epoch training after sparse-feature removal.
statements.problem: The numbers match, but the undefined Epochs column does not establish useful-training endpoints or an extension from epoch 2.
